title: Career Roadmap: Business Analyst
summary: A Business Analyst (BA) identifies business problems, understands stakeholder requirements, analyses information and recommends solutions that improve business performance.

facts.Current degree: BS (4-Year Bachelor of Science - IIT / IISc / Online & Research-oriented)

about.label: Primary Workplaces
about.text: IT companies, consulting firms, banks, fintech companies, startups and product organisations

about.label: Career Focus
about.text: Business requirements, data analysis, process improvement and stakeholder communication

blocks.text: A Business Analyst (BA) identifies business problems, understands stakeholder requirements, analyses information and recommends solutions that improve business performance.
Business Analysts often work between business teams and technical teams, translating business needs into clear requirements for developers, product managers, data teams and other stakeholders.

A BS in Data Science & Applications can provide a useful foundation in data analysis, statistics, programming and visualisation. Students should complement it with business analysis methods, requirements gathering and practical projects.
The exact curriculum and duration depend on the institution and programme structure. The following is a suggested learning roadmap, not a prescribed IIT curriculum.

rows.text: Mathematics, statistics, programming fundamentals and communication
Analyse simple datasets and write business observations
SQL, Python, databases, data visualisation and business fundamentals
Create dashboards and perform exploratory data analysis
Business process modelling, requirements gathering, software development lifecycle and project management
Document business requirements and map existing processes
Advanced analytics, experimentation, domain knowledge and capstone projects
Build an end-to-end business analysis portfolio
Realistic business problem-solving and stakeholder documentation
Complete a business case, requirements document and KPI dashboard

items.text: Gather and clarify requirements from business stakeholders.
Identify operational problems and opportunities for improvement.
Analyse business data, trends, KPIs and performance gaps.
Prepare Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) and functional specifications where required.
Create process maps, workflows, user stories and acceptance criteria.
Coordinate with developers, testers, product managers and business teams.
Support user acceptance testing (UAT) and verify whether solutions meet requirements.

blocks.text: Start with Excel, SQL, Power BI, requirements documentation and Jira. Add other tools based on the roles you target.
Build projects that demonstrate both analytical ability and business thinking.

rows.text: Analyse revenue, profit, regions, products and monthly trends
Identify customer segments associated with higher churn
Examine the purchase funnel and recommend improvements
Analyse applications, interviews, offers and placement conversion
Identify delays, bottlenecks and process inefficiencies
Analyse order delays, cancellations and customer satisfaction
Convert a business problem into user stories, acceptance criteria and a process map

blocks.text: For every project, include the business problem, assumptions, data sources, analysis, findings, recommended actions and measurable success criteria. Avoid presenting a dashboard without explaining the decisions it supports.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: E-commerce Sales and Conversion Improvement
Sales are increasing, but the proportion of website visitors who complete a purchase is low.
Use SQL and Excel to analyse sessions, cart additions, completed orders, revenue and cancellations.
Determine which funnel stages, customer segments or devices show the largest drop-offs.
Write user stories, acceptance criteria, proposed changes and business rules for the checkout improvement.
Compare conversion rate, cart abandonment and revenue before and after implementation, controlling for other changes where possible.

blocks.label: Portfolio deliverables
blocks.text: SQL queries, cleaned dataset, dashboard, process map, BRD or requirements specification, user stories, recommendations and a short presentation.
Look for internships that combine business problem-solving with data or software projects.

blocks.label: Early stage
blocks.text: Excel reporting, SQL exercises, data cleaning and business case studies.

blocks.label: Intermediate stage
blocks.text: Power BI dashboards, KPI analysis, documentation and process mapping.

blocks.label: Internship stage
blocks.text: Business Analyst Intern, Data Analyst Intern, Product Analyst Intern or Operations Analyst Intern.

blocks.label: Final stage
blocks.text: Own a small analysis project from requirement gathering to recommendations and stakeholder presentation.
When applying, demonstrate that you can explain why an analysis matters to the business, not just how to create a chart.

rows.text: Stakeholder requirements, process analysis and specifications
Data extraction, analysis, reporting and insights
Dashboards, KPI reporting and data modelling
Process efficiency, costs and performance metrics
Product usage, funnels, engagement and experimentation
Recurring reports, data validation and business metrics
Business problem-solving, analysis and client deliverables
Requirements and configuration for a specific business system

blocks.text: A Data Science degree may also qualify you for data-focused roles. The exact eligibility depends on employer requirements and the skills demonstrated.
Choose certifications based on the role and tools required by target employers.

rows.text: IIBA Entry Certificate in Business Analysis (ECBA), after checking current eligibility and requirements
Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst (PL-300) certification
Structured SQL courses with practical assessments
Scrum fundamentals or an appropriate Agile certification
BPMN and business process analysis courses
CAPM or foundational project management training, if relevant

blocks.text: Certifications are optional for many entry-level roles. Prioritise practical projects, analytical reasoning, documentation and interview preparation.

items.text: MBA in Business Analytics, Information Systems, Operations or Strategy.
Master's degree in Business Analytics or Information Systems.
Advanced study in Data Science or Applied Statistics.
Specialised training in product management, financial analysis or process improvement.

blocks.text: A postgraduate degree is not mandatory for most entry-level Business Analyst positions if the candidate already meets the employer's educational and skill requirements.
Stage 1 — Intern / Graduate Analyst
Supports reporting, research, documentation and basic analysis.
Stage 2 — Business Analyst
Manages requirements, maps processes and works with stakeholders on defined projects.
Stage 3 — Senior Business Analyst / Lead Analyst
Leads complex analysis, mentors junior analysts and manages cross-functional requirements.
Stage 4 — Business Analysis Manager / Product Manager / Consultant
Leads teams, shapes business solutions or moves into product, consulting or strategy roles.
Progression varies by company, industry, performance and whether the candidate follows a business, data, product or consulting pathway.

blocks.label: AI-enabled business analysis
blocks.text: Using AI to organise requirements and accelerate documentation, with human review.

blocks.label: Data-driven decision-making
blocks.text: Combining SQL, dashboards and statistical reasoning to evaluate business performance.

blocks.label: Process automation
blocks.text: Identifying workflows suitable for automation and measuring the results.

blocks.label: Product analytics
blocks.text: Analysing customer journeys, engagement, retention and conversion.

blocks.label: Cloud and digital transformation
blocks.text: Supporting migration, system implementation and changes to business processes.

blocks.label: Privacy and responsible data use
blocks.text: Ensuring analysis and reporting respect data governance and access restrictions.

blocks.label: Agile delivery
blocks.text: Translating changing business needs into prioritised, testable requirements.

By the end of the degree and practical training, the candidate should be able to:

items.text: Translate business problems into structured analytical questions.
Use SQL and spreadsheets to investigate business data.
Build dashboards that communicate meaningful KPIs.
Gather stakeholder requirements and document functional needs.
Map workflows and recommend improvements based on evidence.
Collaborate with technical teams, business users and project managers.
Present findings clearly and explain their business implications.

blocks.label: Recommended pathway
blocks.text: Build a strong foundation in SQL, Excel, Power BI and business requirements analysis; complete an end-to-end portfolio project; and pursue internships that expose you to real stakeholders and business decisions.
